To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the NUE concept is suitable to describe NUE of crops in greenhouse and field, and to rank varieties in NUE, UN, EN,g, and CN,g.

NUE of spring wheat varieties was similar in greenhouse and field experiments, but the ranking of varieties differed regarding N uptake efficiency (higher in greenhouse) and grain-specific N efficiency and grain N concentration.

the NUE concept is useful for describing and integrating important NUE components of crops grown in different environments and treatments, and that the NUE ranking of varieties is stable in different experimental set-ups.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new concept for NUE assessment of crops and its validation in field and greenhouse.

the development and application of a new concept for NUE of crops, including the entire crop life cycle, and with the evaluation of the concept’s usefulness for assessing NUE of crops grown in different environments and treatments.
the development of a new concept for NUE assessment of plants and the evaluation of the concept by testing it with contrasting wheat varieties grown in field and controlled conditions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NUE concept can be used for assessment of crop NUE in different environments, but with some caution regarding the ranking of varieties regarding N and yield production efficiency.
the new concept for assessment NUE is a promising approach to describe the crop’s response to different treatments and environmental conditions.
the concept is promising for future studies on NUE, but more research is needed to validate the concept and to identify its limitations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NUE was higher in the varieties with higher yield potential and higher N use potential.
the NUE concept is useful for comparing varieties, and that the concept is robust in different environments.
the greenhouse is a suitable set-up for screening for NUE in spring wheat varieties, but the ranking of varieties for EN,g and CN is not stable across environments.
The main takeaway from our work is that
NUE of spring wheat is affected by both environmental factors and variety characteristics, and that these factors can be disentangled with the NUE concept.
the new plant-based NUE concept is applicable in different environments.
NUE of crops can be assessed with a plant based NUE concept, and that NUE is a useful trait for selection of wheat varieties.
